name: Chebyshev Real-Valued Lower Bound on π(2n)

problemStatement.formal: For all n >= 1, prove (n * log 4 - log (2n + 1)) / log (2n) <= Nat.primeCounting (2n), and combine it with the matching Chebyshev upper estimate to obtain explicit pi(x) = Theta(x / log x) bounds.
problemStatement.plain: Turn Chebyshev's integer power inequalities into an explicit real-valued lower bound for the prime-counting function at 2n.
whyMatters: Completes the Chebyshev bridge from binomial coefficient estimates to prime-counting bounds.
Makes the lower constant explicit enough to pair with the existing upper-bound proof.
Documents a historically important route toward the prime number theorem without analytic machinery.

proven: Proofs/ChebyshevPNTBridgeOQ02.lean proves chebyshev_lower_log, chebyshev_lower_real, chebyshev_lower_pos, and chebyshev_pi_interval.

The lower bound plus the existing upper bound gives an explicit Chebyshev interval for pi(2n) with constants log 2 and 2 * log 4.
open: Tightening the lower constant from log 2 toward Chebyshev's original 0.921 remains future work.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Proved (n·log4 − log(2n+1))/log(2n) ≤ π(2n) for n ≥ 1. Four theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
insights: The lower bound chains two sandwich inequalities via log: 4^n ≤ (2n+1)·C(2n,n) ≤ (2n+1)·(2n)^π(2n).
Taking log and rearranging gives n·log4 - log(2n+1) ≤ π(2n)·log(2n), then dividing by log(2n) > 0.
The bound is always non-vacuous: 4^n > 2n+1 for all n ≥ 1, proved by elementary induction (base 4>3; step 2k+3 < 4(2k+1) ≤ 4·4^k).
For large n, the lower bound grows as n·log(4)/log(2n) ~ log(2)·(n/log n), confirming π(x) ≳ log(2)·(x/log x).
The upper bound (from Erdos31PrimesDensity) and this lower bound together give the complete Chebyshev interval log(2) ≤ π(2n)·log(2n)/n ≤ 2·log(4) + o(1).
